title: As You Like It: True/False, Event Ordering, and Comprehension Questions on Extracts
summary: Three sets of exercises on extracts from As You Like It: deciding whether statements about Orlando and Rosalind are true or false, putting four events in chronological order, and answering five comprehension questions about the characters' actions in the forest.

title: Arrange Orlando's Speech Lines in Order and Imagine an Alternative Scene Ending
summary: Students rearrange scrambled lines from Orlando's romantic speech about writing verses on the trees, then rewrite a short paragraph imagining how Orlando might react differently if Rosalind revealed herself in another way.

title: As You Like It: Order Events and Answer Comprehension Questions on Phoebe's Encounter
summary: Students order four events involving Phoebe, Silvius, and Rosalind disguised as Ganymede, then answer seven comprehension questions about why Phoebe runs from Silvius and how Ganymede responds to her confession of love.

title: Match Characters with Actions, Compare Old and Modern English, and Write as Phoebe
summary: Students match four characters to what they did in the scene, identify modern equivalents of old English words in the original extracts, and write a short letter from Phoebe confessing her love to Ganymede.

title: As You Like It: Multiple Choice and True/False Exercises on Orlando's Rescue of Oliver
summary: Students choose correct answers from six multiple-choice questions and judge five statements true or false, both based on extracts about Orlando saving Oliver from a lioness and the aftermath involving Rosalind and Ganymede.

title: Order Key Events, Complete a Summary, and Write a Letter as Oliver to Frederick
summary: Students finish two remaining true/false statements, put six events from the rescue scene in order, fill in a summary about Oliver and Orlando's reunion using modern English words, then write a letter as Oliver to Frederick.

title: As You Like It: True/False, Character Matching, and Comprehension on the Final Scene
summary: Students judge six statements about the play's resolution true or false, match six characters with their relationships or actions, and answer four questions about what Hymen says to the couples in the final gathering.

title: Complete Comprehension, Reorder Jacques' Speech, and Write a Letter as Duke Frederick
summary: Students answer a fifth comprehension question about Duke Frederick's actions, arrange scrambled lines from Jacques' speech summarising the play's ending, and write a letter as Duke Frederick explaining his decision to become a holy man.
